Form text nearly invisible in dark mode — FIXED** (`bd39dc6`): root cause was `src/app/globals.css`'s leftover default-Next.js-template `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block, which flipped `body`'s `color` to `#ededed` (near-white) whenever a visitor's OS was in dark mode. Every component in this app uses explicit light-mode Tailwind classes (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`, etc.) — nothing else in the codebase actually reads `--background`/`--foreground` (confirmed via grep, zero other matches) — so this was a genuinely half-implemented, unused dark-mode remnant. Any element that doesn't set its own explicit text color (the login/signup email/password inputs, specifically) inherited that near-white body color and rendered on a white input background — nearly invisible, exactly matching the report ("kadang ga keliatan sama sekali"). Removed the dark-mode block entirely rather than patch around it, since there's no real dark-mode design to preserve. Verified in browser: forced dark `prefers-color-scheme` via `resize_window`'s `colorScheme` param, confirmed `getComputedStyle` on the email input showed `color: rgb(23,23,23)` (dark, readable) instead of the old near-white — fix holds regardless of visitor OS theme.
16	
17	**3. General "lemot"/slow feeling on the live site — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED** (`414cf01`): user confirmed this is specifically about slow **initial page load** (not post-load interaction lag) on the deployed production site. Measured via `curl -w`: homepage TTFB ~0.65s warm, ~1.6s cold before the fix — not catastrophic but not fast.
18	
19	**Root cause found and fixed for the homepage specifically**: `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s `updateSession()` already calls `supabase.auth.getUser()` on every request (necessary — refreshes the session per Supabase's documented Next.js pattern), and `src/app/page.tsx`'s `Home` Server Component was **independently calling `getUser()` again** — a second Auth-API round-trip on the critical path of every single homepage load, purely to decide whether to redirect an already-logged-in visitor to `/dashboard`. Swapped to `getSession()` (reads the already-refreshed cookie locally, no network call) since this specific check is a UX nicety, not a real access-control boundary.
20	
21	**Deliberately left alone** (audited via `grep supabase.auth.getUser` — 7 total call sites): `middleware.ts` itself (must stay `getUser()`, that's the one that actually refreshes the cookie), `business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` (real subscription/access gate), `dashboard/page.tsx` and `admin/page.tsx` (list/show real per-user data), `onboarding/actions.ts` and `billing/actions.ts` (mutations tied to a specific authenticated user, e.g. payments) — all of these need the server-validated `getUser()`, swapping them to `getSession()` would weaken real security checks, not just an optimization.
22	
23	**Full-app E2E sweep 2026-07-17** (user asked "cek keseluruhan dari fitur-fitur"): committed the previously-stuck receipt auto-print fix (`386ed41` — classifier outage had blocked the commit the day before), then ran statics (41/41 vitest, tsc, eslint all clean) and a full browser walkthrough on the fresh Dev DB: new admin-API-created user (`claude.test.dev@example.com` / `test-kasirku-dev-123`, business "Toko Test Dev" id `b93a088f-15c3-4147-b29a-1342235ab855`, activated to `lifetime` via service-role) → onboarding → billing gate → product+cashier creation → POS PIN → shift open → cash checkout with change → receipt (auto-print confirmed: the print dialog opening is what blocks the Browser-pane renderer — that hang is the success signal, recover by navigating away) → journal auto-posting → every accounting/SDM/ops page (all 200) → all public pages (all 200). Kembalian contrast fix from `af06d94` visually confirmed via computed style (value lab-lightness ~8 vs label ~48, weight 700).
24	
25	**New bug found and fixed during the sweep** (`d662a6c`): "today" was computed as the **UTC** date (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`) in 13 files — between 00:00–07:00 WIB this points at *yesterday*. Symptom that exposed it: Neraca defaulted to showing all zeros minutes after a sale posted at 00:04 WIB. Affected: Neraca + Rekonsiliasi default as-of dates, form date prefills (jurnal manual, kas harian, invoice baru, expense, receivable, purchase), member validity checks (3 member pages), ticket-report active-member count, Excel export Neraca cutoff. Fixed via new shared `src/lib/wib.ts` → `todayWibDateString()` (the `en-CA`+`Asia/Jakarta` pattern the already-correct pages used). **Rule for future code on this project: never `toISOString().slice(0,10)` for "today" — always `todayWibDateString()`.**
26	
27	**Not yet done / open**: this only speeds up the homepage's own redundant check — it does NOT address whatever the dashboard, POS, or other pages' first-load latency looks like (each has its own render path and hasn't been profiled). Also unexplored: Vercel cold-start latency, Supabase query latency inside the dashboard/business pages (some report pages do multiple sequential queries), and client-side bundle size. **How to apply**: if "lemot" persists after this homepage fix, next ask specifically *which* page(s) still feel slow to open (dashboard? POS? a report page?) and profile that page's own request waterfall rather than assuming the same getUser()-duplication pattern is the cause everywhere — it was confirmed only for the homepage.
28	
29	**Round 2, 2026-07-19 — accounting pages specifically, DONE** (user reported "input transaksi jurnal" and other menus feel slow). Investigation agent found: jurnal/neraca/laba-rugi/arus-kas/dashboard-home each ran 3-4 independent Supabase queries sequentially (`await` one after another) instead of `Promise.all`; worse, `arus-kas`'s opening-cash-balance calculation ran a **second full unbounded history scan of every account's journal lines** (no lower date bound, by design — but not filtered to just the Kas account either) on every page load. Fixed:
30	- `jurnal`, `neraca`, `laba-rugi` page.tsx: business/accounts/entries(/reversals) queries parallelized via `Promise.all` (were sequential).
31	- `arus-kas/page.tsx`: business+accounts parallelized; the opening-balance query now uses `journal_lines!inner(...)` + `.eq("journal_lines.account_id", kasAccountId)` so Postgres filters to just Kas-account lines server-side instead of shipping every account's lines over the wire — and that query now runs in parallel with the period's entries query instead of before it.
32	- Dashboard home (`(dashboard)/page.tsx`): business/expenses/openShift parallelized (transactions query still has to wait, since its table name depends on `business.business_type`).
33	- Verified E2E on the Dev DB test account ([[test-account-preview]]): all 4 pages render correct, cross-consistent numbers (Kas & Bank Rp15.000 in Neraca matches Saldo Kas Akhir in Arus Kas across "Semua"/"Bulan Ini"/"Hari Ini" period filters — the "Hari Ini" case is the one that actually exercises the new filtered opening-balance query, since it's the only filter where prior-period activity exists to test against). `tsc`/`eslint` clean, no console errors.
34	- **Tooling gotcha hit again**: after editing these 5 files, all 5 routes 404'd until **two** full `preview_stop` + `rm -rf .next` + `preview_start` cycles — one wasn't enough. Matches the exact same Turbopack-on-slow-drive flakiness already documented above for new route folders; apparently editing files inside an existing `(dashboard)` route group can trigger it too, not just adding new folders.
35	- **Not yet done**: query result sizes still unbounded for large/old businesses (no `.limit()`, "Semua" period has no date bound at all, JS-side aggregation instead of SQL `SUM`) — acceptable for now since real businesses on this product are still small, but will matter once a business has months of transaction history. Revisit if "lemot" is reported again after data volume grows.

If this ever needs re-checking, that's the gap.

**2. Form text nearly invisible in dark mode — FIXED** (`bd39dc6`): root cause was `src/app/globals.css`'s leftover default-Next.js-template `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block, which flipped `body`'s `color` to `#ededed` (near-white) whenever a visitor's OS was in dark mode. Every component in this app uses explicit light-mode Tailwind classes (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`, etc.) — nothing else in the codebase actually reads `--background`/`--foreground` (confirmed via grep, zero other matches) — so this was a genuinely half-implemented, unused dark-mode remnant. Any element that doesn't set its own explicit text color (the login/signup email/password inputs, specifically) inherited that near-white body color and rendered on a white input background — nearly invisible, exactly matching the report ("kadang ga keliatan sama sekali"). Removed the dark-mode block entirely rather than patch around it, since there's no real dark-mode design to preserve. Verified in browser: forced dark `prefers-color-scheme` via `resize_window`'s `colorScheme` param, confirmed `getComputedStyle` on the email input showed `color: rgb(23,23,23)` (dark, readable) instead of the old near-white — fix holds regardless of visitor OS theme.

**3. General "lemot"/slow feeling on the live site — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED** (`414cf01`): user confirmed this is specifically about slow **initial page load** (not post-load interaction lag) on the deployed production site. Measured via `curl -w`: homepage TTFB ~0.65s warm, ~1.6s cold before the fix — not catastrophic but not fast.

**Root cause found and fixed for the homepage specifically**: `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s `updateSession()` already calls `supabase.auth.getUser()` on every request (necessary — refreshes the session per Supabase's documented Next.js pattern), and `src/app/page.tsx`'s `Home` Server Component was **independently calling `getUser()` again** — a second Auth-API round-trip on the critical path of every single homepage load, purely to decide whether to redirect an already-logged-in visitor to `/dashboard`. Swapped to `getSession()` (reads the already-refreshed cookie locally, no network call) since this specific check is a UX nicety, not a real access-control boundary.

**Deliberately left alone** (audited via `grep supabase.auth.getUser` — 7 total call sites): `middleware.ts` itself (must stay `getUser()`, that's the one that actually refreshes the cookie), `business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` (real subscription/access gate), `dashboard/page.tsx` and `admin/page.tsx` (list/show real per-user data), `onboarding/actions.ts` and `billing/actions.ts` (mutations tied to a specific authenticated user, e.g. payments) — all of these need the server-validated `getUser()`, swapping them to `getSession()` would weaken real security checks, not just an optimization.

**Full-app E2E sweep 2026-07-17** (user asked "cek keseluruhan dari fitur-fitur"): committed the previously-stuck receipt auto-print fix (`386ed41` — classifier outage had blocked the commit the day before), then ran statics (41/41 vitest, tsc, eslint all clean) and a full browser walkthrough on the fresh Dev DB: new admin-API-created user (`claude.test.dev@example.com` / `test-kasirku-dev-123`, business "Toko Test Dev" id `b93a088f-15c3-4147-b29a-1342235ab855`, activated to `lifetime` via service-role) → onboarding → billing gate → product+cashier creation → POS PIN → shift open → cash checkout with change → receipt (auto-print confirmed: the print dialog opening is what blocks the Browser-pane renderer — that hang is the success signal, recover by navigating away) → journal auto-posting → every accounting/SDM/ops page (all 200) → all public pages (all 200). Kembalian contrast fix from `af06d94` visually confirmed via computed style (value lab-lightness ~8 vs label ~48, weight 700).

Symptom that exposed it: Neraca defaulted to showing all zeros minutes after a sale posted at 00:04 WIB. Affected: Neraca + Rekonsiliasi default as-of dates, form date prefills (jurnal manual, kas harian, invoice baru, expense, receivable, purchase), member validity checks (3 member pages), ticket-report active-member count, Excel export Neraca cutoff. **Not yet done / open**: this only speeds up the homepage's own redundant check — it does NOT address whatever the dashboard, POS, or other pages' first-load latency looks like (each has its own render path and hasn't been profiled). 1. `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts` — what does `buildKitchenPrintJobs` do today (signature, inputs, what it queries, what it returns)? Does it still exist, or was it renamed/restructured?
2. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts` — read the full file. How does `dispatchPrintJobs`/`dispatchOne` work today (LAN via print-agent HTTP relay, LAN/Bluetooth via native Capacitor plugin, web fallback)? What happens on failure today — is there ANY persistence/retry, or does it just report failure via `logKitchenPrintFailures`?
3. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` — find `checkout()` and `updateSelfOrderStatus()` (or wherever kitchen print jobs get built today) — confirm how they call `buildKitchenPrintJobs`/similar, and what data (product categories, items) feeds into it. 4. `src/lib/offline-queue.ts` and `src/lib/offline-db.ts` — read fully. This is the existing IndexedDB-based retry-queue pattern used for offline checkout retry (pending_sales store). I want to know its exact shape (types, functions: enqueueSale, listPending, markSyncing, markSynced, markError, discardPending) so a NEW similar queue for failed print jobs can mirror this pattern consistently.
5. `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts` — read fully, this is the polling/retry hook for the sale queue (retries every 20s when pending exist, on 'online' event, etc). I want to replicate this pattern for print job retries.
6. Where does the transaction detail page live (`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` or similar) — what data does it already have available (transaction_items, categories) that a "reprint to kitchen/bar" button would need? Is `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` already imported/used anywhere near there (e.g. for the "Cetak ke <printer>" receipt button pattern added recently)?
7. Check `kitchen_printers` table columns currently in use (grep migrations under supabase/migrations for "kitchen_printers") — confirm current columns (id, name, categories, connection_type, address, device_label, prints_receipt, anything else).

# Reprint kitchen ticket + auto-retry when printer comes back online

## Context
Kitchen/bar printing (`src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`) is currently pure best-effort: `dispatchPrintJobs` tries each job once, and on failure just writes an activity-log warning via `logKitchenPrintFailures` — the job itself is dropped, nothing retries it, and there's no way to resend a ticket for a transaction that already happened. User wants two things fixed together: (1) a manual "cetak ulang ke dapur/bar" button on a past transaction, and (2) tickets that failed because a printer was off should print automatically once it's back on, not require someone to notice and manually redo it.

## Approach
Both features share one new piece of infrastructure: a client-side IndexedDB retry queue for failed print jobs, mirroring the existing offline-sale-queue pattern (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts` + `offline-db.ts` + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts`) already proven in this codebase. `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) is already fully self-contained — the rendered ESC/POS bytes are right there — so a failed job can be persisted and resent verbatim later with zero server round-trip needed for the retry itself.

## Implementation

**1. `src/lib/offline-db.ts`** — bump `DB_VERSION` to 3, add a `pending_prints` store (keyPath `id`, index `by-business` same as `pending_sales`).

**2. New `src/lib/print-queue.ts`** — mirrors `offline-queue.ts` exactly:
```ts
type PendingPrintJob = {
  id: string; businessId: string; createdAt: string;
  attempts: number; status: "pending" | "error"; errorMessage?: string;
  job: KitchenPrintJobPayload;
};
```
`enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)`, `listPendingPrints(businessId)`, `markPrintSynced(id)` (delete), `markPrintAttempt(pendingJob, error)` (increments `attempts`, sets `errorMessage`; past 15 attempts flips `status` to `"error"` so auto-retry stops and it needs the manual button), `discardPendingPrint(id)`.

**3. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`**:
- `dispatchPrintJobs`: on any failed job, `enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)` in addition to the existing `logKitchenPrintFailures` call (unchanged) — this is the single entry point every caller already goes through (checkout, self-order, receipt reprint, kitchen reprint), so no caller-side changes needed for jobs to start being retried.
- New `retryPendingPrintJobs(businessId)`: lists pending prints, calls the existing `dispatchOne` for each (already exported-equivalent logic, just needs `dispatchOne` exported instead of module-private), `markPrintSynced` on success (log one activity line "struk/tiket berhasil dicetak setelah percobaan ulang" only on the transition to success, not every poll), `markPrintAttempt` on failure. Does **not** call `logKitchenPrintFailures` on every retry attempt (would spam the activity log every ~20s) — only logs once when a job's attempts are exhausted and it flips to `"error"`.

**4. New `src/hooks/use-print-retry.ts`** — mirrors `use-offline-sync.ts`'s polling shape: tracks `pendingPrints` state, retries every 20s (same `SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` the sale queue uses) while any are pending, plus on the `online` event, guarded by a ref against overlapping runs.

**5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** — mount `usePrintRetry(businessId)` next to the existing `useOfflineSync`. Add a small status pill next to `OfflineStatus` (same visual language: amber while retrying, red + count once any job hits `"error"` and needs the manual reprint button) so the cashier isn't left guessing whether a failed kitchen ticket is being handled.

**6. Reprint button — new files**:
   - `transactions/actions.ts`: new `buildKitchenReprintJobs(businessId, transactionId)` — reads `transaction_items` (`name, category, qty` — category is already stored per line at sale time, no need to re-join `products`), calls the existing `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, { source: "Cetak Ulang", label: invoiceNumber, items })` from `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`, returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (already fanned out to every matching printer — same routing checkout uses, no per-printer picker needed in the UI).
   - New `transactions/[transactionId]/reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (client component, same shape as the existing `receipt/print-button.tsx`'s per-printer buttons): one "🍳 Cetak Ulang ke Dapur/Bar" button, calls the action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)`, shows ✅/❌ inline. Not gated on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` — LAN jobs work from a plain browser too via the print-agent relay, same as checkout's auto-print already does.
   - Wire into `transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` next to the existing `VoidTransactionForm`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, open a past transaction, click reprint, confirm a job is attempted (LAN via print-agent won't have a real printer here, so it'll fail — that's fine, use it to prove the failure gets queued).
- Confirm via `javascript_tool` reading IndexedDB (`kasirku-offline` v3, `pending_prints` store) that the failed job was persisted with the transaction's data.
- Confirm the POS screen's retry pill appears and that `retryPendingPrintJobs` gets called on the next interval (check `read_network_requests` for the server-action POST, or console-log presence) without spamming `logActivity` on every cycle.
- No printer hardware in this environment — full end-to-end "printer was off, comes back on, ticket appears" needs the user's own hardware to confirm once deployed, same caveat as prior printer work.

User wants two things fixed together: (1) a manual "cetak ulang ke dapur/bar" button on a past transaction, and (2) tickets that failed because a printer was off should print automatically once it's back on, not require someone to notice and manually redo it.

## Approach
Both features share one new piece of infrastructure: a client-side IndexedDB retry queue for failed print jobs, mirroring the existing offline-sale-queue pattern (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts` + `offline-db.ts` + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts`) already proven in this codebase. `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) is already fully self-contained — the rendered ESC/POS bytes are right there — so a failed job can be persisted and resent verbatim later with zero server round-trip needed for the retry itself.

**2. New `src/lib/print-queue.ts`** — mirrors `offline-queue.ts` exactly:
```ts
type PendingPrintJob = {
  id: string; businessId: string; createdAt: string;
  attempts: number; status: "pending" | "error"; errorMessage?: string;
  job: KitchenPrintJobPayload;
};
```
`enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)`, `listPendingPrints(businessId)`, `markPrintSynced(id)` (delete), `markPrintAttempt(pendingJob, error)` (increments `attempts`, sets `errorMessage`; past 15 attempts flips `status` to `"error"` so auto-retry stops and it needs the manual button), `discardPendingPrint(id)`.

**3. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`**:
- `dispatchPrintJobs`: on any failed job, `enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)` in addition to the existing `logKitchenPrintFailures` call (unchanged) — this is the single entry point every caller already goes through (checkout, self-order, receipt reprint, kitchen reprint), so no caller-side changes needed for jobs to start being retried.
- New `retryPendingPrintJobs(businessId)`: lists pending prints, calls the existing `dispatchOne` for each (already exported-equivalent logic, just needs `dispatchOne` exported instead of module-private), `markPrintSynced` on success (log one activity line "struk/tiket berhasil dicetak setelah percobaan ulang" only on the transition to success, not every poll), `markPrintAttempt` on failure. Does **not** call `logKitchenPrintFailures` on every retry attempt (would spam the activity log every ~20s) — only logs once when a job's attempts are exhausted and it flips to `"error"`.

**4. New `src/hooks/use-print-retry.ts`** — mirrors `use-offline-sync.ts`'s polling shape: tracks `pendingPrints` state, retries every 20s (same `SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` the sale queue uses) while any are pending, plus on the `online` event, guarded by a ref against overlapping runs.

**5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** — mount `usePrintRetry(businessId)` next to the existing `useOfflineSync`. Add a small status pill next to `OfflineStatus` (same visual language: amber while retrying, red + count once any job hits `"error"` and needs the manual reprint button) so the cashier isn't left guessing whether a failed kitchen ticket is being handled.

**6. Reprint button — new files**:
   - `transactions/actions.ts`: new `buildKitchenReprintJobs(businessId, transactionId)` — reads `transaction_items` (`name, category, qty` — category is already stored per line at sale time, no need to re-join `products`), calls the existing `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, { source: "Cetak Ulang", label: invoiceNumber, items })` from `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`, returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (already fanned out to every matching printer — same routing checkout uses, no per-printer picker needed in the UI).
   - New `transactions/[transactionId]/reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (client component, same shape as the existing `receipt/print-button.tsx`'s per-printer buttons): one "🍳 Cetak Ulang ke Dapur/Bar" button, calls the action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)`, shows ✅/❌ inline.    - Wire into `transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` next to the existing `VoidTransactionForm`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, open a past transaction, click reprint, confirm a job is attempted (LAN via print-agent won't have a real printer here, so it'll fail — that's fine, use it to prove the failure gets queued).
- Confirm via `javascript_tool` reading IndexedDB (`kasirku-offline` v3, `pending_prints` store) that the failed job was persisted with the transaction's data.
- Confirm the POS screen's retry pill appears and that `retryPendingPrintJobs` gets called on the next interval (check `read_network_requests` for the server-action POST, or console-log presence) without spamming `logActivity` on every cycle.
- No printer hardware in this environment — full end-to-end "printer was off, comes back on, ticket appears" needs the user's own hardware to confirm once deployed, same caveat as prior printer work.

# Reprint kitchen ticket + auto-retry when printer comes back online

## Context
Kitchen/bar printing (`src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`) is currently pure best-effort: `dispatchPrintJobs` tries each job once, and on failure just writes an activity-log warning via `logKitchenPrintFailures` — the job itself is dropped, nothing retries it, and there's no way to resend a ticket for a transaction that already happened. User wants two things fixed together: (1) a manual "cetak ulang ke dapur/bar" button on a past transaction, and (2) tickets that failed because a printer was off should print automatically once it's back on, not require someone to notice and manually redo it.

## Approach
Both features share one new piece of infrastructure: a client-side IndexedDB retry queue for failed print jobs, mirroring the existing offline-sale-queue pattern (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts` + `offline-db.ts` + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts`) already proven in this codebase. `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) is already fully self-contained — the rendered ESC/POS bytes are right there — so a failed job can be persisted and resent verbatim later with zero server round-trip needed for the retry itself.

## Implementation

**1. `src/lib/offline-db.ts`** — bump `DB_VERSION` to 3, add a `pending_prints` store (keyPath `id`, index `by-business` same as `pending_sales`).

**2. New `src/lib/print-queue.ts`** — mirrors `offline-queue.ts` exactly:
```ts
type PendingPrintJob = {
  id: string; businessId: string; createdAt: string;
  attempts: number; status: "pending" | "error"; errorMessage?: string;
  job: KitchenPrintJobPayload;
};
```
`enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)`, `listPendingPrints(businessId)`, `markPrintSynced(id)` (delete), `markPrintAttempt(pendingJob, error)` (increments `attempts`, sets `errorMessage`; past 15 attempts flips `status` to `"error"` so auto-retry stops and it needs the manual button), `discardPendingPrint(id)`.

**3. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`**:
- `dispatchPrintJobs`: on any failed job, `enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)` in addition to the existing `logKitchenPrintFailures` call (unchanged) — this is the single entry point every caller already goes through (checkout, self-order, receipt reprint, kitchen reprint), so no caller-side changes needed for jobs to start being retried.
- New `retryPendingPrintJobs(businessId)`: lists pending prints, calls the existing `dispatchOne` for each (already exported-equivalent logic, just needs `dispatchOne` exported instead of module-private), `markPrintSynced` on success (log one activity line "struk/tiket berhasil dicetak setelah percobaan ulang" only on the transition to success, not every poll), `markPrintAttempt` on failure. Does **not** call `logKitchenPrintFailures` on every retry attempt (would spam the activity log every ~20s) — only logs once when a job's attempts are exhausted and it flips to `"error"`.

**4. New `src/hooks/use-print-retry.ts`** — mirrors `use-offline-sync.ts`'s polling shape: tracks `pendingPrints` state, retries every 20s (same `SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` the sale queue uses) while any are pending, plus on the `online` event, guarded by a ref against overlapping runs.

**5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** — mount `usePrintRetry(businessId)` next to the existing `useOfflineSync`. Add a small status pill next to `OfflineStatus` (same visual language: amber while retrying, red + count once any job hits `"error"` and needs the manual reprint button) so the cashier isn't left guessing whether a failed kitchen ticket is being handled.

**6. Reprint button — new files**:
   - `transactions/actions.ts`: new `buildKitchenReprintJobs(businessId, transactionId)` — reads `transaction_items` (`name, category, qty` — category is already stored per line at sale time, no need to re-join `products`), calls the existing `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, { source: "Cetak Ulang", label: invoiceNumber, items })` from `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`, returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (already fanned out to every matching printer — same routing checkout uses, no per-printer picker needed in the UI).
   - New `transactions/[transactionId]/reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (client component, same shape as the existing `receipt/print-button.tsx`'s per-printer buttons): one "🍳 Cetak Ulang ke Dapur/Bar" button, calls the action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)`, shows ✅/❌ inline. Not gated on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` — LAN jobs work from a plain browser too via the print-agent relay, same as checkout's auto-print already does.
   - Wire into `transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` next to the existing `VoidTransactionForm`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, open a past transaction, click reprint, confirm a job is attempted (LAN via print-agent won't have a real printer here, so it'll fail — that's fine, use it to prove the failure gets queued).
- Confirm via `javascript_tool` reading IndexedDB (`kasirku-offline` v3, `pending_prints` store) that the failed job was persisted with the transaction's data.
- Confirm the POS screen's retry pill appears and that `retryPendingPrintJobs` gets called on the next interval (check `read_network_requests` for the server-action POST, or console-log presence) without spamming `logActivity` on every cycle.
- No printer hardware in this environment — full end-to-end "printer was off, comes back on, ticket appears" needs the user's own hardware to confirm once deployed, same caveat as prior printer work.

---
name: offline-pos-phase1
description: "Mode offline kasir (POS) Fase 1 — resiliensi mid-session, built 2026-07-13"
metadata:
  type: project
  originSessionId: current
---

Dibangun 2026-07-13: kasir bisa tetap jualan kalau internet toko putus **saat halaman POS sudah terbuka & shift aktif** (scope disepakati dengan user — bukan cold-start offline/PWA penuh, itu belum ada infra sama sekali dan didokumentasikan sebagai Fase 2 terpisah). Lihat [[mini-erp-scope]] untuk histori fitur lain, [[supabase-migrations-manual]] untuk cara apply migrasi.

**Arsitektur**: `src/lib/offline-db.ts` (wrapper IndexedDB native) + `src/lib/offline-queue.ts` (tipe `PendingSale`, enqueue/list/mark helpers, `pendingStockDeltas`) + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts` (hook dipakai `pos-screen.tsx` & `ticket-pos-screen.tsx` — tracking online/offline, retry berurutan, auto-sync tiap 20 detik / saat event `online`). `handleConfirmPayment` di kedua layar membungkus `checkout()`/`checkoutTicket()` dengan `withTimeout` (`src/lib/with-timeout.ts`, 10 detik) — timeout atau exception jaringan masuk antrian offline (IndexedDB), business error (mis. uang kurang, nomor tiket bentrok) tetap tampil error inline seperti biasa.

**Idempotency**: migrasi `supabase/migrations/20260713100000_offline_checkout_idempotency.sql` menambah `client_ref uuid` (unique per business, partial index) ke `transactions` & `ticket_transactions`, plus param `p_client_ref` di `checkout_transaction`/`checkout_ticket_transaction` — kalau client_ref sudah ada, RPC return baris lama (`already_existed=true`) alih-alih insert duplikat. **Applied ke Supabase 2026-07-13** (bareng `20260712160000_ticket_group_pricing.sql`, lihat [[supabase-migrations-manual]] untuk detail & gotcha saat apply). Kode client selalu mengirim `p_client_ref` ke kedua RPC (jalur online normal maupun retry offline) — jadi migrasi ini wajib ter-apply duluan sebelum checkout apa pun bisa jalan.

**Verifikasi mekanik offline** (browser, akun test [[test-account-preview]], sebelum migrasi ter-apply — jadi ini menguji jalur "gagal", bukan happy-path): patch `window.fetch` untuk reject di tengah checkout retail (Kopi Susu, Toko Test Laporan) → benar masuk jalur offline, tersimpan ke IndexedDB, stok tampilan langsung berkurang (`pendingStockDeltas` jalan). Antrian **selamat lewat hard page reload** (dipicu tak sengaja oleh polling self-order FnB yang gagal fetch RSC lalu Next fallback ke full navigation) — hook re-mount, baca ulang IndexedDB, tetap ada. Auto-sync 20 detik jalan sendiri, memanggil RPC asli, dapat error PostgREST asli ("Could not find the function...") karena migrasi belum ke-apply saat itu → ditandai `status:error` dengan pesan asli tampil di tooltip pill, bukan retry selamanya — persis sesuai desain "gagal karena bisnis vs jaringan". Tombol "Hapus" di tooltip berhasil membuang item dari antrian, stok tampilan balik normal.

**Verifikasi happy-path setelah migrasi ter-apply (2026-07-13)**: checkout tiket normal (bukan simulasi offline) di `ticket-pos-screen.tsx` sukses dengan invoice asli (`TIX-20260713-0001`), tidak fallback ke jalur offline — konfirmasi `p_client_ref` diterima RPC dengan benar dan `already_existed` flag berfungsi. Belum sempat re-test checkout retail online setelah migrasi (hanya tiket), tapi kode path-nya identik (sama-sama lewat `withTimeout`+`clientRef`), risiko rendah.

**Catatan tooling**: monkeypatch `window.fetch` di JS console TIDAK mencegat request Server Action itu sendiri (Next.js action dispatcher tampaknya pakai referensi fetch yang sudah di-bind lebih awal) — yang kepencet justru RSC prefetch/`router.refresh()` punya `fetch`. Jadi cara paling andal untuk simulasi "checkout gagal jaringan" di test browser berikutnya: biarkan patch aktif SEBELUM klik tombol confirm (bukan setelah), dan jangan kaget kalau retry via `syncNow()` juga sempat gagal karena fetch masih ke-patch — itu justru bukti antrian bekerja, bukan bug.

**How to apply**: migrasi sudah live, tidak ada lagi blocker untuk pakai POS normal. Fase 2 (cold-start offline / PWA / service worker) belum mulai sama sekali, backlog terpisah kalau user minta lanjut.

---
name: offline-pos-phase2
description: "Mode offline kasir Fase 2 — cold-start via Service Worker, built & verified 2026-07-13"
metadata:
  type: project
  originSessionId: current
---

Lanjutan [[offline-pos-phase1]] (mid-session resilience). Fase 2 menutup gap yang sengaja ditunda Fase 1: tab POS yang di-refresh atau dibuka dari kondisi **benar-benar offline** sekarang tetap bisa render, lewat service worker manual (bukan plugin build-time — riset ke `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/progressive-web-apps.md` menemukan opsi resmi Serwist "currently requires webpack configuration", belum jelas kompatibel dengan Turbopack yang dipakai proyek ini).

**Temuan penting soal Next.js 16 di repo ini**: `middleware.ts` sudah tidak dipakai lagi sebagai nama convention — sekarang **`proxy.ts`** (fungsinya identik, cuma nama file/istilah berubah, lihat `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/16-proxy.md`). File root proyek ini: `src/proxy.ts` (memanggil `updateSession` dari `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`, yang nama filenya sendiri TIDAK berubah). Kalau nyari middleware di masa depan, cari `proxy.ts` dulu.

**Arsitektur**: `public/sw.js` (baru, vanilla JS tanpa dependency) — pada event `fetch`, hanya intersep request **GET** yang **same-origin** dan path-nya masuk allowlist (`/_next/static/*`, `/business/*/pos`, `/business/*/pos/check-in`, `/favicon.ico`, `/manifest.webmanifest`); selain itu dibiarkan lewat begitu saja (termasuk semua Server Action yang selalu POST — jadi checkout Fase 1 sama sekali tidak tersentuh SW). # Reprint kitchen ticket + auto-retry when printer comes back online

## Context
Kitchen/bar printing (`src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`) is currently pure best-effort: `dispatchPrintJobs` tries each job once, and on failure just writes an activity-log warning via `logKitchenPrintFailures` — the job itself is dropped, nothing retries it, and there's no way to resend a ticket for a transaction that already happened. User wants two things fixed together: (1) a manual "cetak ulang ke dapur/bar" button on a past transaction, and (2) tickets that failed because a printer was off should print automatically once it's back on, not require someone to notice and manually redo it.

## Approach
Both features share one new piece of infrastructure: a client-side IndexedDB retry queue for failed print jobs, mirroring the existing offline-sale-queue pattern (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts` + `offline-db.ts` + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts`) already proven in this codebase. `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) is already fully self-contained — the rendered ESC/POS bytes are right there — so a failed job can be persisted and resent verbatim later with zero server round-trip needed for the retry itself.

## Implementation

**1. `src/lib/offline-db.ts`** — bump `DB_VERSION` to 3, add a `pending_prints` store (keyPath `id`, index `by-business` same as `pending_sales`).

**2. New `src/lib/print-queue.ts`** — mirrors `offline-queue.ts` exactly:
```ts
type PendingPrintJob = {
  id: string; businessId: string; createdAt: string;
  attempts: number; status: "pending" | "error"; errorMessage?: string;
  job: KitchenPrintJobPayload;
};
```
`enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)`, `listPendingPrints(businessId)`, `markPrintSynced(id)` (delete), `markPrintAttempt(pendingJob, error)` (increments `attempts`, sets `errorMessage`; past 15 attempts flips `status` to `"error"` so auto-retry stops and it needs the manual button), `discardPendingPrint(id)`.

**3. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`**:
- `dispatchPrintJobs`: on any failed job, `enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)` in addition to the existing `logKitchenPrintFailures` call (unchanged) — this is the single entry point every caller already goes through (checkout, self-order, receipt reprint, kitchen reprint), so no caller-side changes needed for jobs to start being retried.
- New `retryPendingPrintJobs(businessId)`: lists pending prints, calls the existing `dispatchOne` for each (already exported-equivalent logic, just needs `dispatchOne` exported instead of module-private), `markPrintSynced` on success (log one activity line "struk/tiket berhasil dicetak setelah percobaan ulang" only on the transition to success, not every poll), `markPrintAttempt` on failure. Does **not** call `logKitchenPrintFailures` on every retry attempt (would spam the activity log every ~20s) — only logs once when a job's attempts are exhausted and it flips to `"error"`.

**4. New `src/hooks/use-print-retry.ts`** — mirrors `use-offline-sync.ts`'s polling shape: tracks `pendingPrints` state, retries every 20s (same `SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` the sale queue uses) while any are pending, plus on the `online` event, guarded by a ref against overlapping runs.

**5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** — mount `usePrintRetry(businessId)` next to the existing `useOfflineSync`. Add a small status pill next to `OfflineStatus` (same visual language: amber while retrying, red + count once any job hits `"error"` and needs the manual reprint button) so the cashier isn't left guessing whether a failed kitchen ticket is being handled.

**6. Reprint button — new files**:
   - `transactions/actions.ts`: new `buildKitchenReprintJobs(businessId, transactionId)` — reads `transaction_items` (`name, category, qty` — category is already stored per line at sale time, no need to re-join `products`), calls the existing `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, { source: "Cetak Ulang", label: invoiceNumber, items })` from `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`, returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (already fanned out to every matching printer — same routing checkout uses, no per-printer picker needed in the UI).
   - New `transactions/[transactionId]/reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (client component, same shape as the existing `receipt/print-button.tsx`'s per-printer buttons): one "🍳 Cetak Ulang ke Dapur/Bar" button, calls the action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)`, shows ✅/❌ inline. Not gated on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` — LAN jobs work from a plain browser too via the print-agent relay, same as checkout's auto-print already does.
   - Wire into `transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` next to the existing `VoidTransactionForm`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, open a past transaction, click reprint, confirm a job is attempted (LAN via print-agent won't have a real printer here, so it'll fail — that's fine, use it to prove the failure gets queued).
- Confirm via `javascript_tool` reading IndexedDB (`kasirku-offline` v3, `pending_prints` store) that the failed job was persisted with the transaction's data.
- Confirm the POS screen's retry pill appears and that `retryPendingPrintJobs` gets called on the next interval (check `read_network_requests` for the server-action POST, or console-log presence) without spamming `logActivity` on every cycle.
- No printer hardware in this environment — full end-to-end "printer was off, comes back on, ticket appears" needs the user's own hardware to confirm once deployed, same caveat as prior printer work.

# Full-app offline viewing (Fase 3), like Moka POS

## Context
The Android app is a thin Capacitor WebView with no local bundle — every navigation is normally a full network round trip. Two earlier phases (documented in memory as `offline-pos-phase1`/`phase2`) already solved this for the **POS screen specifically**: checkout works fully offline via an IndexedDB retry queue, and a service worker (`public/sw.js`) caches the POS route so it still renders cold from a dead network. That's deliberately narrow — Phase 2's design explicitly excluded every other page ("Neraca, Laporan, dst. sengaja TIDAK disentuh — menampilkan data keuangan basi seolah live itu berbahaya").

User confirmed today, after testing, that the POS-offline behavior works exactly as designed (instant checkout, zero lag) — but tapping into Riwayat Transaksi while offline hits a raw WebView `ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE` page. They want the same "just works offline" experience Moka gives across the **whole app**, financial pages included, and explicitly accepted the stale-data tradeoff I flagged.

**Scope, confirmed with user:** viewing/opening pages offline (like Moka), not full offline editing everywhere — mutations outside the already-built POS checkout queue still require connectivity (auditing/queueing every form app-wide is a much larger, separate effort not what "buka aplikasinya" was asking for).

## Approach
The existing network-first-with-cache-fallback service worker pattern already generalizes cleanly to any GET route — it's just an allowlist regex today. No new architecture needed, three additions:

1. **`public/sw.js`** — broaden `isAllowedPath` from the POS-only regex to any `/business/[businessId]/**` route plus `/dashboard` (keep marketing/auth pages out — not useful offline, no reason to cache them). Bump `CACHE_NAME` (`kasirku-pos-v1` → `kasirku-app-v1`) so the `activate` handler's existing stale-cache purge cleanly evicts the old narrow-scoped cache. Add a navigation fallback: for `request.mode === "navigate"` requests that fail AND aren't already in cache (first-ever offline visit to an uncached page), serve a new cached `/offline` page instead of `Response.error()` — replaces the raw WebView error screen from today's test with something that actually looks like part of the app. Pre-cache `/offline` itself during the `install` event so it's available even before any online visit.

2. **New `src/app/offline/page.tsx`** — minimal static page: "📴 Kamu sedang offline — buka halaman yang sudah pernah dikunjungi sebelumnya, atau coba lagi setelah tersambung." No data fetching (must render standalone with zero network).

3. **Move SW registration app-wide + add a visible offline banner**:
   - New small client component `src/app/service-worker-register.tsx` (registration logic already exists in `use-offline-sync.ts:117-121` for POS-only mounting — move/duplicate that `navigator.serviceWorker.register(...)` call here instead) — mounted in root `src/app/layout.tsx` so it registers on first load of *any* page, not just after visiting POS first (today's gap: someone who opens Riwayat before ever opening POS has no cache yet).
   - New `src/app/offline-banner.tsx` (client component, `navigator.onLine` + `online`/`offline` listeners, same pattern as the existing POS `OfflineStatus` but app-wide and read-only — no queue/retry UI, just a fixed top banner "📴 Offline — data yang ditampilkan mungkin bukan yang terbaru") — mounted next to the SW register component in root layout. This is the key mitigation for the stale-financial-data risk: it's now visually unmistakable when a page might be showing old numbers, on every page, not just POS.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Queueing mutations (Simpan Bon edits outside checkout, Pengaturan changes, journal entries, etc.) for offline retry — stays online-only, same as today; attempting one while offline will just show a normal network-error message from that action's existing error handling, not a new failure mode.
- Per-page "last synced at HH:MM" timestamps — the app-wide banner is the mitigation, not per-page metadata (would touch far more files for marginal benefit).
- Ticket-venue-specific pages (`ticket-pos-screen.tsx` already has its own SW registration call sharing `use-offline-sync.ts` — leaving that as-is, the broadened `isAllowedPath` covers its routes too since they're under `/business/[businessId]/`).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, visit a few pages (POS, Riwayat Transaksi, Pengaturan, a report page) to populate cache, confirm via `javascript_tool` that `caches.open('kasirku-app-v1')` contains them.
- Stop the dev server (`preview_stop`) to simulate total network death, reload each previously-visited page — confirm full render from cache (mirrors the Phase 2 "server benar-benar mati" test already proven for POS).
- Reload a route that was **never** visited this session while the server is still down — confirm the new `/offline` page renders instead of a raw connection-error screen.
- Confirm the offline banner appears/disappears correctly by toggling `navigator.onLine`-driven events (or actually stopping/starting the dev server) — not just present on POS but on a backoffice page too.
- Restart the server, confirm a normal online page load still gets fresh data (network-first isn't broken) and no console/server errors.
- Real end-to-end "open the Android app with the phone in airplane mode" needs the user's own device to confirm, same caveat as every prior offline/printer round.

Kitchen/bar printing (`src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`) is currently pure best-effort: `dispatchPrintJobs` tries each job once, and on failure just writes an activity-log warning via `logKitchenPrintFailures` — the job itself is dropped, nothing retries it, and there's no way to resend a ticket for a transaction that already happened. User wants two things fixed together: (1) a manual "cetak ulang ke dapur/bar" button on a past transaction, and (2) tickets that failed because a printer was off should print automatically once it's back on, not require someone to notice and manually redo it.

## Approach
Both features share one new piece of infrastructure: a client-side IndexedDB retry queue for failed print jobs, mirroring the existing offline-sale-queue pattern (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts` + `offline-db.ts` + `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts`) already proven in this codebase. `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) is already fully self-contained — the rendered ESC/POS bytes are right there — so a failed job can be persisted and resent verbatim later with zero server round-trip needed for the retry itself.

## Implementation

**1. `src/lib/offline-db.ts`** — bump `DB_VERSION` to 3, add a `pending_prints` store (keyPath `id`, index `by-business` same as `pending_sales`).

**2. New `src/lib/print-queue.ts`** — mirrors `offline-queue.ts` exactly:
```ts
type PendingPrintJob = {
  id: string; businessId: string; createdAt: string;
  attempts: number; status: "pending" | "error"; errorMessage?: string;
  job: KitchenPrintJobPayload;
};
```
`enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)`, `listPendingPrints(businessId)`, `markPrintSynced(id)` (delete), `markPrintAttempt(pendingJob, error)` (increments `attempts`, sets `errorMessage`; past 15 attempts flips `status` to `"error"` so auto-retry stops and it needs the manual button), `discardPendingPrint(id)`.

**3. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`**:
- `dispatchPrintJobs`: on any failed job, `enqueuePrintJob(businessId, job)` in addition to the existing `logKitchenPrintFailures` call (unchanged) — this is the single entry point every caller already goes through (checkout, self-order, receipt reprint, kitchen reprint), so no caller-side changes needed for jobs to start being retried.
- New `retryPendingPrintJobs(businessId)`: lists pending prints, calls the existing `dispatchOne` for each (already exported-equivalent logic, just needs `dispatchOne` exported instead of module-private), `markPrintSynced` on success (log one activity line "struk/tiket berhasil dicetak setelah percobaan ulang" only on the transition to success, not every poll), `markPrintAttempt` on failure. Does **not** call `logKitchenPrintFailures` on every retry attempt (would spam the activity log every ~20s) — only logs once when a job's attempts are exhausted and it flips to `"error"`.

**4. New `src/hooks/use-print-retry.ts`** — mirrors `use-offline-sync.ts`'s polling shape: tracks `pendingPrints` state, retries every 20s (same `SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` the sale queue uses) while any are pending, plus on the `online` event, guarded by a ref against overlapping runs.

**5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** — mount `usePrintRetry(businessId)` next to the existing `useOfflineSync`. Add a small status pill next to `OfflineStatus` (same visual language: amber while retrying, red + count once any job hits `"error"` and needs the manual reprint button) so the cashier isn't left guessing whether a failed kitchen ticket is being handled.

**6. Reprint button — new files**:
   - `transactions/actions.ts`: new `buildKitchenReprintJobs(businessId, transactionId)` — reads `transaction_items` (`name, category, qty` — category is already stored per line at sale time, no need to re-join `products`), calls the existing `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, { source: "Cetak Ulang", label: invoiceNumber, items })` from `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`, returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (already fanned out to every matching printer — same routing checkout uses, no per-printer picker needed in the UI).
   - New `transactions/[transactionId]/reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (client component, same shape as the existing `receipt/print-button.tsx`'s per-printer buttons): one "🍳 Cetak Ulang ke Dapur/Bar" button, calls the action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)`, shows ✅/❌ inline. Not gated on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` — LAN jobs work from a plain browser too via the print-agent relay, same as checkout's auto-print already does.
   - Wire into `transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` next to the existing `VoidTransactionForm`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, open a past transaction, click reprint, confirm a job is attempted (LAN via print-agent won't have a real printer here, so it'll fail — that's fine, use it to prove the failure gets queued).
- Confirm via `javascript_tool` reading IndexedDB (`kasirku-offline` v3, `pending_prints` store) that the failed job was persisted with the transaction's data.
- Confirm the POS screen's retry pill appears and that `retryPendingPrintJobs` gets called on the next interval (check `read_network_requests` for the server-action POST, or console-log presence) without spamming `logActivity` on every cycle.
- No printer hardware in this environment — full end-to-end "printer was off, comes back on, ticket appears" needs the user's own hardware to confirm once deployed, same caveat as prior printer work.

# Full-app offline viewing (Fase 3), like Moka POS

## Context
The Android app is a thin Capacitor WebView with no local bundle — every navigation is normally a full network round trip. Two earlier phases (documented in memory as `offline-pos-phase1`/`phase2`) already solved this for the **POS screen specifically**: checkout works fully offline via an IndexedDB retry queue, and a service worker (`public/sw.js`) caches the POS route so it still renders cold from a dead network. That's deliberately narrow — Phase 2's design explicitly excluded every other page ("Neraca, Laporan, dst. sengaja TIDAK disentuh — menampilkan data keuangan basi seolah live itu berbahaya").

User confirmed today, after testing, that the POS-offline behavior works exactly as designed (instant checkout, zero lag) — but tapping into Riwayat Transaksi while offline hits a raw WebView `ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE` page. They want the same "just works offline" experience Moka gives across the **whole app**, financial pages included, and explicitly accepted the stale-data tradeoff I flagged.

**Scope, confirmed with user:** viewing/opening pages offline (like Moka), not full offline editing everywhere — mutations outside the already-built POS checkout queue still require connectivity (auditing/queueing every form app-wide is a much larger, separate effort not what "buka aplikasinya" was asking for).

## Approach
The existing network-first-with-cache-fallback service worker pattern already generalizes cleanly to any GET route — it's just an allowlist regex today. No new architecture needed, three additions:

1. **`public/sw.js`** — broaden `isAllowedPath` from the POS-only regex to any `/business/[businessId]/**` route plus `/dashboard` (keep marketing/auth pages out — not useful offline, no reason to cache them). Bump `CACHE_NAME` (`kasirku-pos-v1` → `kasirku-app-v1`) so the `activate` handler's existing stale-cache purge cleanly evicts the old narrow-scoped cache. Add a navigation fallback: for `request.mode === "navigate"` requests that fail AND aren't already in cache (first-ever offline visit to an uncached page), serve a new cached `/offline` page instead of `Response.error()` — replaces the raw WebView error screen from today's test with something that actually looks like part of the app. Pre-cache `/offline` itself during the `install` event so it's available even before any online visit.

2. **New `src/app/offline/page.tsx`** — minimal static page: "📴 Kamu sedang offline — buka halaman yang sudah pernah dikunjungi sebelumnya, atau coba lagi setelah tersambung." No data fetching (must render standalone with zero network).

3. **Move SW registration app-wide + add a visible offline banner**:
   - New small client component `src/app/service-worker-register.tsx` (registration logic already exists in `use-offline-sync.ts:117-121` for POS-only mounting — move/duplicate that `navigator.serviceWorker.register(...)` call here instead) — mounted in root `src/app/layout.tsx` so it registers on first load of *any* page, not just after visiting POS first (today's gap: someone who opens Riwayat before ever opening POS has no cache yet).
   - New `src/app/offline-banner.tsx` (client component, `navigator.onLine` + `online`/`offline` listeners, same pattern as the existing POS `OfflineStatus` but app-wide and read-only — no queue/retry UI, just a fixed top banner "📴 Offline — data yang ditampilkan mungkin bukan yang terbaru") — mounted next to the SW register component in root layout. This is the key mitigation for the stale-financial-data risk: it's now visually unmistakable when a page might be showing old numbers, on every page, not just POS.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Queueing mutations (Simpan Bon edits outside checkout, Pengaturan changes, journal entries, etc.) for offline retry — stays online-only, same as today; attempting one while offline will just show a normal network-error message from that action's existing error handling, not a new failure mode.
- Per-page "last synced at HH:MM" timestamps — the app-wide banner is the mitigation, not per-page metadata (would touch far more files for marginal benefit).
- Ticket-venue-specific pages (`ticket-pos-screen.tsx` already has its own SW registration call sharing `use-offline-sync.ts` — leaving that as-is, the broadened `isAllowedPath` covers its routes too since they're under `/business/[businessId]/`).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, visit a few pages (POS, Riwayat Transaksi, Pengaturan, a report page) to populate cache, confirm via `javascript_tool` that `caches.open('kasirku-app-v1')` contains them.
- Stop the dev server (`preview_stop`) to simulate total network death, reload each previously-visited page — confirm full render from cache (mirrors the Phase 2 "server benar-benar mati" test already proven for POS).
- Reload a route that was **never** visited this session while the server is still down — confirm the new `/offline` page renders instead of a raw connection-error screen.
- Confirm the offline banner appears/disappears correctly by toggling `navigator.onLine`-driven events (or actually stopping/starting the dev server) — not just present on POS but on a backoffice page too.
- Restart the server, confirm a normal online page load still gets fresh data (network-first isn't broken) and no console/server errors.
- Real end-to-end "open the Android app with the phone in airplane mode" needs the user's own device to confirm, same caveat as every prior offline/printer round.

content.thinking:
So they're clarifying their actual need—the KASIR app specifically needs to work offline without internet, and the performance should feel equally responsive whether connected or not, rather than requiring the entire app to be offline-capable.

Looking back at what's been built, the POS screen already handles this through the local-first architecture: it renders instantly from the cached IndexedDB data, checkout operations queue offline and sync later, and kitchen print retries work. The speed improvements from caching should already satisfy the "equally snappy" requirement.

I should ask what specifically isn't working—whether opening the POS app cold from the icon in airplane mode is failing, or if there's a particular interaction that feels slow or broken offline.

Actually, I'm realizing the real bottleneck: the Capacitor config hardcodes the entry point to `/login` on every cold app launch, regardless of whether the user has an active session. That means even if they're already logged in and just want to jump straight to POS, the app forces them through the login screen first—and `/login` probably isn't cached for offline access, so it would fail immediately without internet. So the real problem is that when the service worker doesn't intercept /login (because it's deliberately excluded from the allowlist), the request passes straight through to the browser, which hits the native connection error page if offline — and since Capacitor always launches to /login on cold start, users can never get past that native error screen to reach any cached POS pages, no matter how good the offline caching is. The gap is that the app's entry point itself requires network. I'm considering whether to change the Capacitor config to point somewhere that's either cached or redirects intelligently instead of /login...

Actually, the cleanest fix is to add /login to the service worker's cache allowlist with the same network-first-cache-fallback strategy, then make the /login Server Component smarter: if a valid session already exists in the cookie, it redirects immediately to /dashboard without needing a server round trip. This way the entry point works offline, and users get routed to their last-used screen automatically if they're already authenticated. The real issue might be that the `/login` page itself is a Server Component calling `supabase.auth.getUser()`, so even a cached response would just replay whatever redirect decision was made last time — which should be fine since sessions persist. The practical fix is straightforward: add `/login` to the service worker allowlist and verify the login page's current redirect behavior for authenticated users, then implement the change quickly.

The `/login` page is a pure Client Component without server-side redirects, so authenticated users who navigate there just see the login form again instead of being automatically redirected elsewhere. I'm wondering whether there's actually any logic in place to redirect already-authenticated users away from the login page.

The real problem is that `/login` isn't in the Service Worker's cache allowlist, so when offline, the browser can't even load the login page's HTML shell and JavaScript bundle on first request — the Service Worker doesn't intercept it since it's excluded, and the user just sees a native connection error before React can mount. Adding `/login` to the Service Worker's allowed paths would let a cold, cache-primed device load the login page offline, but then there's still the question of what happens if a session cookie already exists — the cached login page won't automatically know to redirect them to the dashboard.

The solution is to add `/login` to the Service Worker's cache allowlist, then modify the login page component to check on mount whether a valid session already exists locally using `supabase.auth.getSession()`, which reads from localStorage synchronously without needing a network request, and if one does exist, immediately redirect to the dashboard. Skipping the auto-redirect-to-last-POS feature for now since the core issue is just getting the app to open offline at all — reaching /dashboard is already a major win and keeps things simple. content.thinking:
The user says buttons still aren't showing even after reloading, so I'm considering why the service worker might not be updating the cached offline page. The standard service worker lifecycle keeps a new version in a waiting state until all old tabs close, but our code calls `skipWaiting()` during install, which should force immediate activation and bypass that delay.

However, there's a timing issue: when the user "opens the app online," that page is still controlled by the old service worker instance until the new one activates and claims control. Even though `clients.claim()` runs during activation, any requests already in flight from the old page were handled by the old worker. The real problem might be that Capacitor's WebView cold-launches fresh at `/login` each time the app opens, which should be a clean navigation that goes through the new service worker—but something in that flow isn't working as expected.

Actually, I think I found the bug: I reused the same cache name "kasirku-app-v1" for this offline-page-buttons fix without bumping the version. When the new service worker installs, it calls `cache.addAll(["/offline","/login"])`, which should fetch fresh copies from the network and overwrite the old cached entries for those URLs. That should work correctly even with the same cache name, since `cache.addAll()` does fetch fresh and `put()` into the cache, overwriting existing entries.

But here's the real issue — the install event only fires if the service worker file itself has changed byte-for-byte. Since I only modified the Next.js offline page in this commit and didn't touch `public/sw.js`, the browser sees the SW file as identical to before and never re-runs the install event. This means `/offline` never gets re-fetched or re-cached, so the user sees the stale version.

So when the router tries to fetch that RSC payload while offline and it's not cached under the exact request signature, the service worker returns `Response.error()` for non-navigate requests, which causes the underlying fetch to reject and throw a network error. content.thinking:
So the connection logic tries the secure socket approach first, and if that throws an IOException, it falls back to the insecure variant. The issue is that on many Android devices, especially with certain printer models, the secure BluetoothSocket.connect() call can hang indefinitely—or more precisely, it times out after around 12 seconds before throwing the exception that triggers the fallback.

For cheap thermal printers like the RPP02N that don't implement proper secure pairing or bonding, the secure attempt will always fail slowly, which explains the 15-second delay we're seeing. The printer eventually connects via the insecure fallback, but only after wasting time on the failed secure attempt.

The core fix would be to prioritize the insecure connection for thermal printers instead of trying secure first, since these devices rarely support secure pairing anyway and secure is what's causing the multi-second hangs. There's already evidence in the code that some printer stacks reject secure connections entirely, so flipping the priority to insecure-first for this printer class makes sense.

Since this is a native Android change in Kotlin, I'll need to rebuild the APK and have you reinstall it — similar to the cancelDiscovery() fix we did earlier. The implementation involves reordering the socket creation calls to attempt the insecure connection first and fall back to secure only if that fails.

Regarding the queue notification issue — since the print actually succeeds after 15 seconds rather than failing, no queue entry gets created by design. The real complaint is about not seeing progress during that wait. Once we fix the Bluetooth latency by swapping the connection order, that 15-second delay should mostly disappear anyway. cd "G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu" && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Try insecure Bluetooth RFCOMM first, fixing ~15s print delay

Cheap ESC/POS thermal printers (confirmed on RPP02N) essentially never
support Bluetooth's secure/authenticated RFCOMM. Trying secure first meant
every single print paid Android's ~12s BluetoothSocket.connect() timeout
before falling back to the insecure socket that actually works — showing
up as checkout/kitchen tickets taking ~15 seconds to print, with no
explanation to the cashier. Swapped the order: insecure first, secure as
the fallback for any printer that genuinely needs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

I'm settling on the approach: EDC needs to be added as a built-in payment method alongside the existing ones like Tunai and QRIS, so it can be treated as a standard settlement option rather than a custom addition. The settlement report's existing grouping logic already handles whatever payment method strings exist in the database, so "Kartu" would naturally appear as its own line without forcing a rename to "EDC" — this is actually more flexible and matches how real settlements work. But the user did explicitly request "EDC," so I need to check what they actually want before deciding whether to add it as a new built-in method or just rely on the existing aggregation.

Now I'm thinking through the shift-close settlement report feature itself — when a cashier closes their shift, they should be able to print a settlement breakdown showing totals by payment method (Tunai, QRIS, Kartu/EDC, etc.), and this needs to integrate into the existing close_shift flow in the POS screen.

But the user also wants broader reporting capability — they want to print settlement reports and menu sales reports for any chosen date, not just at the moment of shift close. Since the reports page already has date-range filtering built in, I should leverage that existing infrastructure and add the print functionality there, while also providing a quick one-tap print option right at shift close for convenience. I'm realizing the shift-scoped approach gets complicated since the reports system is purely date-based without shift filtering, and multiple shifts can happen on the same day. The cleaner solution is to keep settlement and menu report printing date-based throughout, then at shift close, pass the shift's opened_at and closed_at timestamps as a custom date range into the reports print action so it captures exactly that shift's transactions.

I can create reusable ESC/POS builders for settlement and menu tickets that accept an explicit from/to ISO date range, matching the same period system the Reports page uses — this way the same builders work whether called from the Reports page for any period or from shift close for that specific shift's window.

Building the report print utilities... Finishing the settlement query logic, then building a menu sales print job that groups transaction items by name to sum quantities and amounts. I'll also create a new client component with two print buttons that let users select which kitchen printer to send the reports to, reusing the existing printer selection pattern.

For the settlement report specifically, I'm thinking it makes sense to auto-target whichever printer has `prints_receipt = true` since that's the cashier printer and the natural destination for settlement data meant for the owner. This keeps it simple—one tap, no picker UI needed—and matches how customer receipts already work. If no receipt printer is configured, I'll show a friendly message instead.

Then I'm wiring these buttons into the reports page by passing the date range down, and adding a shortcut at shift-close so users can print the settlement right after closing out their shift.

For the shift-close shortcut, I'm keeping it straightforward: since tracking the exact shift open/close timestamps client-side would add complexity, I'll just print the settlement for today's date range rather than trying to pass the shift's specific timestamps through.

Actually, there's a cleaner approach — I can create a shift-specific settlement function that filters transactions directly by `shift_id` instead of relying on date ranges. This avoids the ambiguity of multiple shifts happening on the same day and gives me precise data for that shift. ## Context
User wants two new printable reports, closer to what Moka POS gives at shift close: a **settlement** report (Tunai/QRIS/EDC totals) and a **menu sales** report (item/qty sold) — both printable for any transaction date range, not just tied to a live shift. `close_shift`'s RPC only computes a cash-vs-non-cash split (`shift_rpc.sql:53-133`), and there's no per-method breakdown or print action anywhere in the codebase today (the shift-receipt route from an earlier now-reverted session doesn't exist). The Reports page (`reports/page.tsx`) already computes both aggregations in-memory for its date-filtered view (`byMethod` map, `menuSales` map) and already has CSV/Excel export buttons — that's the natural place to add "print" as a third export option, plus a convenience shortcut right after closing a shift.

Confirmed with user: "Kartu" is renamed to "EDC" (same slot, no schema change — old transactions keep showing "Kartu" as their recorded method, new ones record "EDC"); both reports auto-print to whichever printer(s) are flagged `prints_receipt` in Settings (same target as customer receipts), no printer picker needed.

## Approach

**1. Rename payment method label** — `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS` in `pos-screen.tsx:91` and its duplicate in `ticket-pos-screen.tsx`: `"Kartu"` → `"EDC"`.

**2. `src/lib/escpos.ts`** — two new ESC/POS ticket builders, following `buildReceiptTicket`'s existing shape/helpers (`padLine`, `RECEIPT_WIDTH`):
   - `buildSettlementTicket({businessName, periodLabel, byMethod: {method, amount}[], totalSales, txCount, voidCount})` — "LAPORAN SETTLEMENT" header, one line per payment method + total, tx/void counts.
   - `buildMenuSalesTicket({businessName, periodLabel, items: {name, qty, amount}[], totalQty, totalAmount})` — "LAPORAN PENJUALAN MENU" header, one line per item, sorted by amount desc (matches Reports page's existing "Menu Terlaris" ordering).

**3. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-actions.ts`** (business-level, not inside `(dashboard)` or `pos/`, so both can import it) — two server actions:
   - `buildSettlementPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   - `buildMenuSalesPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   
   Each: finds `kitchen_printers` where `prints_receipt = true` (same query shape as `buildReceiptPrintJobsForTransaction` in `pos/actions.ts`), queries `transaction_payments`/`transaction_items` joined to `transactions` filtered by business+date range+`voided = false` (same filter pattern already used in `reports/page.tsx:92-101`), aggregates in JS (mirror the page's existing `byMethod`/`menuSales` reduce logic so the printed numbers always match what's on screen), builds one ticket via the new builders, and returns one `KitchenPrintJobPayload` per matching printer. Empty printer list → `{success:true, jobs:[]}`, handled as a "no printer configured" message client-side (same pattern as the existing reprint button's empty state).

**4. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-buttons.tsx`** (client component, shared) — takes `businessId`, `fromIso`, `toIsoExclusive` as props, renders two buttons ("🖨️ Cetak Settlement", "🖨️ Cetak Laporan Menu"), each calling its action then `dispatchPrintJobs` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs`, inline ✅/❌ state per button — same established pattern as `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx`.

**5. Wire into `reports/page.tsx`** — add `<ReportPrintButtons businessId={businessId} fromIso={fromIso} toIsoExclusive={toIsoExclusive} />` in a new small card right above/alongside the existing "⬇️ Ekspor Data" card, reusing the `fromIso`/`toIsoExclusive` already computed there via `getPeriodRange` — this alone satisfies "bisa cetak berdasarkan tanggal transaksi" for both reports, using the same date-range UI (Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua/Kustom) already on that page.

**6. Wire a shortcut into `pos-screen.tsx`'s shift-close success screen** (`closedSummary` block) — same `<ReportPrintButtons>`, scoped to "today" via `getPeriodRange("today")` imported from `reports/period.ts` (same WIB-correct day-boundary helper the Reports page already uses, avoids reinventing date math). This is a convenience shortcut, not shift-exact scoping (if a business runs multiple shifts same day, this prints the whole day, not just that shift — acceptable given the user's own framing centers on "berdasarkan tanggal transaksi", and the Reports page remains available for any other exact range).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser (dev test account): confirm "EDC" now shows at checkout instead of "Kartu". Configure a `prints_receipt` printer (mirroring earlier verified LAN/Bluetooth test flow), do a transaction, then hit both new print buttons on the Reports page — confirm a job gets built for the configured printer (will fail/queue in this environment since there's no real printer, same limitation as all prior printer testing this session — that's fine, proves the build+dispatch path).
- Confirm the numbers in the printed ticket's underlying aggregation match what's already shown on-screen for the same period (spot-check the byMethod/menuSales sums).
- Confirm the shift-close screen's shortcut buttons appear after closing a shift and target today's date range correctly.
