# Full-app offline viewing (Fase 3), like Moka POS

## Context
The Android app is a thin Capacitor WebView with no local bundle — every navigation is normally a full network round trip. Two earlier phases (documented in memory as `offline-pos-phase1`/`phase2`) already solved this for the **POS screen specifically**: checkout works fully offline via an IndexedDB retry queue, and a service worker (`public/sw.js`) caches the POS route so it still renders cold from a dead network. That's deliberately narrow — Phase 2's design explicitly excluded every other page ("Neraca, Laporan, dst. sengaja TIDAK disentuh — menampilkan data keuangan basi seolah live itu berbahaya").

User confirmed today, after testing, that the POS-offline behavior works exactly as designed (instant checkout, zero lag) — but tapping into Riwayat Transaksi while offline hits a raw WebView `ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE` page. They want the same "just works offline" experience Moka gives across the **whole app**, financial pages included, and explicitly accepted the stale-data tradeoff I flagged.

**Scope, confirmed with user:** viewing/opening pages offline (like Moka), not full offline editing everywhere — mutations outside the already-built POS checkout queue still require connectivity (auditing/queueing every form app-wide is a much larger, separate effort not what "buka aplikasinya" was asking for).

## Approach
The existing network-first-with-cache-fallback service worker pattern already generalizes cleanly to any GET route — it's just an allowlist regex today. No new architecture needed, three additions:

1. **`public/sw.js`** — broaden `isAllowedPath` from the POS-only regex to any `/business/[businessId]/**` route plus `/dashboard` (keep marketing/auth pages out — not useful offline, no reason to cache them). Bump `CACHE_NAME` (`kasirku-pos-v1` → `kasirku-app-v1`) so the `activate` handler's existing stale-cache purge cleanly evicts the old narrow-scoped cache. Add a navigation fallback: for `request.mode === "navigate"` requests that fail AND aren't already in cache (first-ever offline visit to an uncached page), serve a new cached `/offline` page instead of `Response.error()` — replaces the raw WebView error screen from today's test with something that actually looks like part of the app. Pre-cache `/offline` itself during the `install` event so it's available even before any online visit.

2. **New `src/app/offline/page.tsx`** — minimal static page: "📴 Kamu sedang offline — buka halaman yang sudah pernah dikunjungi sebelumnya, atau coba lagi setelah tersambung." No data fetching (must render standalone with zero network).

3. **Move SW registration app-wide + add a visible offline banner**:
   - New small client component `src/app/service-worker-register.tsx` (registration logic already exists in `use-offline-sync.ts:117-121` for POS-only mounting — move/duplicate that `navigator.serviceWorker.register(...)` call here instead) — mounted in root `src/app/layout.tsx` so it registers on first load of *any* page, not just after visiting POS first (today's gap: someone who opens Riwayat before ever opening POS has no cache yet).
   - New `src/app/offline-banner.tsx` (client component, `navigator.onLine` + `online`/`offline` listeners, same pattern as the existing POS `OfflineStatus` but app-wide and read-only — no queue/retry UI, just a fixed top banner "📴 Offline — data yang ditampilkan mungkin bukan yang terbaru") — mounted next to the SW register component in root layout. This is the key mitigation for the stale-financial-data risk: it's now visually unmistakable when a page might be showing old numbers, on every page, not just POS.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Queueing mutations (Simpan Bon edits outside checkout, Pengaturan changes, journal entries, etc.) for offline retry — stays online-only, same as today; attempting one while offline will just show a normal network-error message from that action's existing error handling, not a new failure mode.
- Per-page "last synced at HH:MM" timestamps — the app-wide banner is the mitigation, not per-page metadata (would touch far more files for marginal benefit).
- Ticket-venue-specific pages (`ticket-pos-screen.tsx` already has its own SW registration call sharing `use-offline-sync.ts` — leaving that as-is, the broadened `isAllowedPath` covers its routes too since they're under `/business/[businessId]/`).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser: log in with the dev test account, visit a few pages (POS, Riwayat Transaksi, Pengaturan, a report page) to populate cache, confirm via `javascript_tool` that `caches.open('kasirku-app-v1')` contains them.
- Stop the dev server (`preview_stop`) to simulate total network death, reload each previously-visited page — confirm full render from cache (mirrors the Phase 2 "server benar-benar mati" test already proven for POS).
- Reload a route that was **never** visited this session while the server is still down — confirm the new `/offline` page renders instead of a raw connection-error screen.
- Confirm the offline banner appears/disappears correctly by toggling `navigator.onLine`-driven events (or actually stopping/starting the dev server) — not just present on POS but on a backoffice page too.
- Restart the server, confirm a normal online page load still gets fresh data (network-first isn't broken) and no console/server errors.
- Real end-to-end "open the Android app with the phone in airplane mode" needs the user's own device to confirm, same caveat as every prior offline/printer round.

# Printable shift settlement + menu sales report (by date)

## Context
User wants two new printable reports, closer to what Moka POS gives at shift close: a **settlement** report (Tunai/QRIS/EDC totals) and a **menu sales** report (item/qty sold) — both printable for any transaction date range, not just tied to a live shift. `close_shift`'s RPC only computes a cash-vs-non-cash split (`shift_rpc.sql:53-133`), and there's no per-method breakdown or print action anywhere in the codebase today (the shift-receipt route from an earlier now-reverted session doesn't exist). The Reports page (`reports/page.tsx`) already computes both aggregations in-memory for its date-filtered view (`byMethod` map, `menuSales` map) and already has CSV/Excel export buttons — that's the natural place to add "print" as a third export option, plus a convenience shortcut right after closing a shift.

Confirmed with user: "Kartu" is renamed to "EDC" (same slot, no schema change — old transactions keep showing "Kartu" as their recorded method, new ones record "EDC"); both reports auto-print to whichever printer(s) are flagged `prints_receipt` in Settings (same target as customer receipts), no printer picker needed.

## Approach

**1. Rename payment method label** — `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS` in `pos-screen.tsx:91` and its duplicate in `ticket-pos-screen.tsx`: `"Kartu"` → `"EDC"`.

**2. `src/lib/escpos.ts`** — two new ESC/POS ticket builders, following `buildReceiptTicket`'s existing shape/helpers (`padLine`, `RECEIPT_WIDTH`):
   - `buildSettlementTicket({businessName, periodLabel, byMethod: {method, amount}[], totalSales, txCount, voidCount})` — "LAPORAN SETTLEMENT" header, one line per payment method + total, tx/void counts.
   - `buildMenuSalesTicket({businessName, periodLabel, items: {name, qty, amount}[], totalQty, totalAmount})` — "LAPORAN PENJUALAN MENU" header, one line per item, sorted by amount desc (matches Reports page's existing "Menu Terlaris" ordering).

**3. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-actions.ts`** (business-level, not inside `(dashboard)` or `pos/`, so both can import it) — two server actions:
   - `buildSettlementPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   - `buildMenuSalesPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   
   Each: finds `kitchen_printers` where `prints_receipt = true` (same query shape as `buildReceiptPrintJobsForTransaction` in `pos/actions.ts`), queries `transaction_payments`/`transaction_items` joined to `transactions` filtered by business+date range+`voided = false` (same filter pattern already used in `reports/page.tsx:92-101`), aggregates in JS (mirror the page's existing `byMethod`/`menuSales` reduce logic so the printed numbers always match what's on screen), builds one ticket via the new builders, and returns one `KitchenPrintJobPayload` per matching printer. Empty printer list → `{success:true, jobs:[]}`, handled as a "no printer configured" message client-side (same pattern as the existing reprint button's empty state).

**4. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-buttons.tsx`** (client component, shared) — takes `businessId`, `fromIso`, `toIsoExclusive` as props, renders two buttons ("🖨️ Cetak Settlement", "🖨️ Cetak Laporan Menu"), each calling its action then `dispatchPrintJobs` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs`, inline ✅/❌ state per button — same established pattern as `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx`.

**5. Wire into `reports/page.tsx`** — add `<ReportPrintButtons businessId={businessId} fromIso={fromIso} toIsoExclusive={toIsoExclusive} />` in a new small card right above/alongside the existing "⬇️ Ekspor Data" card, reusing the `fromIso`/`toIsoExclusive` already computed there via `getPeriodRange` — this alone satisfies "bisa cetak berdasarkan tanggal transaksi" for both reports, using the same date-range UI (Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua/Kustom) already on that page.

**6. Wire a shortcut into `pos-screen.tsx`'s shift-close success screen** (`closedSummary` block) — same `<ReportPrintButtons>`, scoped to "today" via `getPeriodRange("today")` imported from `reports/period.ts` (same WIB-correct day-boundary helper the Reports page already uses, avoids reinventing date math). This is a convenience shortcut, not shift-exact scoping (if a business runs multiple shifts same day, this prints the whole day, not just that shift — acceptable given the user's own framing centers on "berdasarkan tanggal transaksi", and the Reports page remains available for any other exact range).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser (dev test account): confirm "EDC" now shows at checkout instead of "Kartu". Configure a `prints_receipt` printer (mirroring earlier verified LAN/Bluetooth test flow), do a transaction, then hit both new print buttons on the Reports page — confirm a job gets built for the configured printer (will fail/queue in this environment since there's no real printer, same limitation as all prior printer testing this session — that's fine, proves the build+dispatch path).
- Confirm the numbers in the printed ticket's underlying aggregation match what's already shown on-screen for the same period (spot-check the byMethod/menuSales sums).
- Confirm the shift-close screen's shortcut buttons appear after closing a shift and target today's date range correctly.

Add printable settlement + menu sales reports, by transaction date

New Moka-style shift settlement report (per-payment-method totals — Tunai/
EDC/QRIS/custom methods) and a menu sales report (item/qty/omzet), both
printable for any transaction date range via two new ESC/POS builders
(buildSettlementTicket, buildMenuSalesTicket in escpos.ts).

Reuses the Reports page's existing date-range system (period/from/to,
already WIB-correct) rather than building parallel filtering — the two new
print buttons live right next to the existing CSV/Excel export buttons
there, and the same buttons appear as a same-day shortcut on the POS
shift-close screen. Both auto-target whichever printer(s) are flagged
prints_receipt, same destination as customer receipts, no picker needed.

Also renamed the "Kartu" payment method to "EDC" (same slot, no schema
change) since that's the actual terminology this maps to.

Verified end-to-end on the dev account: EDC now shows at checkout, an EDC
transaction correctly rolls up into the Reports page's payment-method
breakdown, both new print buttons on the Reports page produce the correct
"no printer configured" empty state (no prints_receipt printer exists in
this test environment) rather than erroring, and the same buttons appear
correctly on the post-shift-close screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

The user's phone still shows the same "KARTU" screen with no settlement report, which points to the familiar caching issue we've seen throughout this conversation—the WebView is serving stale JavaScript from before the deploy. The solution is straightforward: force close the app completely, verify they're online, then reopen it to pull the fresh code.

I'm thinking through the service worker behavior here—since we didn't bump the CACHE_NAME this time, the pages should use network-first caching, meaning they fetch fresh content when online and fall back to cache when offline. But if they're online right now and still seeing the old version, that suggests either the service worker isn't intercepting correctly or the JavaScript bundles haven't updated yet. The force close and reopen should trigger the service worker to refetch everything properly.

The most likely culprit is they haven't actually force-closed and reopened the app since the deploy—the WebView keeps the old JavaScript bundle in memory without re-fetching unless there's a full page reload. I should ask them to explicitly do that, and also verify on our end that the deployment actually succeeded and is live in production.

Looking at the POS Menu panel the user is showing me, I notice there's no "Laporan" option visible — the menu only displays Riwayat Transaksi, Riwayat Shift, Printer Dapur & Bar, Kas Masuk/Keluar, Tutup Shift, and Ganti Kasir. This appears to be a genuine gap where the Android app's cashier-facing POS menu doesn't include the reports link at all.

This is actually intentional by design — the Android app is restricted to POS-only functionality without backoffice access, mirroring a cashier-only role like Moka's. The Reports page lives in the full backoffice sidebar, which the native app deliberately doesn't expose to avoid showing dead-end links that would trigger access denied errors. I should check the pos-screen.tsx menu code to confirm whether there's a conditional check that hides the "Laporan" link specifically for native/Android platforms.

The real problem is that I've placed the settlement/menu print feature on the Reports page, which is unreachable from the Android cashier app — but this feature is fundamentally a POS-level operation (closing the register). I need to either verify why Laporan is hidden in the POS menu and whether it's role-based or always hidden for native, or consider giving this print feature its own dedicated entry point within the POS Menu itself so cashiers can actually access it from the Android app. I could reuse the existing report printing utilities and build a lightweight modal with just a date picker, keeping it simple enough for the native cashier interface. First, I need to look at how the POS menu currently handles native versus web visibility to understand why Reports got excluded and how to properly integrate this new print option.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: The overarching multi-session goal has been making KasirKu (a Next.js 16 POS SaaS app with an Android WebView wrapper via Capacitor) work reliably for real F&B business use, particularly performance and printing. Within the current visible window, the specific chain of user requests was: a. "tambahkan cetak laporan shift saat tutup kasir, jumlah tunai, qris, edc (seperti settlement pada umum nya) bisa samakan dengan Moka, tambahkan juga laporan menu yg terjual, kedua nya bisa cetak berdasarkan tanggal transaksi" — Add a printable shift settlement report (cash/QRIS/EDC totals, Moka-style) and a menu sales report, both printable by transaction date, not just tied to a live shift. b. After clarifying questions (EDC labeling and printer targeting), user chose: "Ganti label 'Kartu' jadi 'EDC'" (rename, same slot) and "Printer yang sama dengan struk pelanggan" (auto-target the prints_receipt printer, no manual picker). c. After implementation, testing, commit, and push, user reported: "di HP blm ada perubahan sama sekali, masih KARTU dan tidak ada settlement nya" — nothing changed on their phone. d. User confirmed they hadn't checked Vercel directly yet; after I found via direct production browser testing that the live site itself (not just their phone) still showed old content, I asked them to check the Vercel dashboard. User agreed: "oke ready" after seeing status. e. User provided a screenshot of the Vercel Deployments list, which revealed the critical bug: the settlement-report commit was completely missing from Vercel's deployment history (dropped webhook, not a build failure). f. After I pushed an empty commit to retrigger deployment, user confirmed "oke ready". g. User asked: "oke untuk cetak ulang laporan shift maupun menu terjual disebelah mana ya ?" — where is the reprint feature located? h. I explained it's on the Reports page (☰ Menu → 📊 Laporan → pick date → 🖨️ Cetak Laporan card). i. User then sent a screenshot of their actual Android app's POS Menu panel, which showed NO "Laporan" option at all (only Riwayat Transaksi, Riwayat Shift, Printer Dapur & Bar, Kas Masuk/Keluar, Tutup Shift, Ganti Kasir), and said: "blm ada laporan" — there's no Laporan option. This last message is the most recent user request and the one actively being worked on: the user needs the settlement/menu report printing feature to actually be reachable from the Android cashier app, where the full "Laporan" backoffice page is deliberately hidden by pre-existing design (Android app is POS-only, no backoffice, per an earlier commit "Restrict the Android app to POS-only, no backoffice, like Moka's Cashier role"). 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Next.js 16 App Router with Server Components/Server Actions, Turbopack dev server - Capacitor WebView wrapping the live Next.js site for the Android app (`android-app/capacitor.config.ts`, `server.url: 'https://createimpact.id/login'`) - ESC/POS thermal printer ticket generation (`src/lib/escpos.ts`) - `KitchenPrintJobPayload` shape (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`) and `dispatchPrintJobs` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs` — the established client-dispatch print pattern - `prints_receipt` boolean flag on `kitchen_printers` table — marks which printer(s) auto-receive customer receipts / now also settlement & menu reports - Date-range period system in `reports/period.ts`: `Period` type (`"today" | "week" | "month" | "all" | "custom"`), `getPeriodRange(period, customFrom?, customTo?)` returning `{fromIso, toIsoExclusive}` in WIB-correct timestamps, `PERIOD_LABELS`, `PERIOD_DESCRIPTIONS` — all pure functions safe for both server and client import - Android app deliberately restricted to POS-only, no backoffice access (existing design decision, commit `9d80161` "Restrict the Android app to POS-only, no backoffice, like Moka's Cashier role") — enforced via `const isNative = Capacitor.isNativePlatform();` gating specific menu links in `pos-screen.tsx` - `pos/printers/page.tsx` pattern: a lightweight, PIN-gated, native-accessible page OUTSIDE the `(dashboard)` route group, used as the template for building new native-reachable cashier-facing pages - Known Turbopack-on-slow-drive bug (documented in project memory): adding a new route folder can make routes 404 until 2 full `preview_stop`/`rm -rf .next`/`preview_start` cycles - Vercel/GitHub webhook deployment: a push can silently fail to trigger a Vercel build (dropped webhook) with no error surfaced anywhere except the Deployments list simply missing that commit; fixed via an empty `git commit --allow-empty` + push to force a fresh webhook event - PIN-based cashier session gating via `getCashierSession(businessId)` + `PinScreen` fallback component 3. Files and Code Sections: - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`** - `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS` changed from `["Tunai", "Kartu", "QRIS"]` to `["Tunai", "EDC", "QRIS"]` - Added `todayRange` computed via `getPeriodRange("today")` (imported from `../(dashboard)/reports/period`), recomputed fresh each render (not memoized) so the WIB day boundary stays correct if the screen stays open past midnight - Added `` to the `closedSummary` (Shift Ditutup) screen, scoped to `todayRange`, with copy: "Cetak laporan hari ini (semua shift, bukan cuma yang baru ditutup):" - In the `☰ Menu` panel: the existing `{!isNative && (...📊 Laporan link to /reports...)}` block was LEFT AS-IS, and immediately after it a NEW link was added (not gated by `isNative`, so visible on both native Android and web): ```tsx setPosMenuOpen(false)} className="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 transition-colors hover:bg-zinc-50" > 🖨️ Cetak Settlement/Menu ``` - Import added: `import ReportPrintButtons from "../report-print-buttons";` and `import { getPeriodRange } from "../(dashboard)/reports/period";` - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/ticket-pos-screen.tsx`** - Same rename: `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS = ["Tunai", "EDC", "QRIS"];` - **`src/lib/escpos.ts`** - Added `buildSettlementTicket(input: SettlementTicketInput): Buffer` — prints "LAPORAN SETTLEMENT" header, period label, per-method amounts (bold TOTAL line), tx/void counts. Types: `SettlementByMethod = {method: string; amount: number}`, `SettlementTicketInput = {businessName, periodLabel, byMethod: SettlementByMethod[], totalSales, txCount, voidCount}`. - Added `buildMenuSalesTicket(input: MenuSalesTicketInput): Buffer` — prints "LAPORAN PENJUALAN MENU" header, period label, per-item qty/amount lines, total qty + bold TOTAL amount. Types: `MenuSalesItem = {name, qty, amount}`, `MenuSalesTicketInput = {businessName, periodLabel, items: MenuSalesItem[], totalQty, totalAmount}`. - Both reuse existing `padLine`, `truncate`, `formatRp`, `formatQty`, `RECEIPT_WIDTH` (32) helpers already in the file from `buildReceiptTicket`. - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-actions.ts`** (NEW file, business-level, sibling to both `pos/` and `(dashboard)/` so both can import it) - `"use server"` directive - `getReceiptPrinters(supabase, businessId)` — queries `kitchen_printers` where `prints_receipt = true` and `address` not null - `toJobs(printers, buffer)` — maps printers + one shared buffer into `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` - `buildSettlementPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive, periodLabel)` — parallel-fetches business name, printers, `transaction_payments` (joined `transactions!inner` filtered by business_id/voided=false/date range) for per-method sums, and `transactions` rows for tx/void counts; builds ticket via `buildSettlementTicket`; returns `{success:true, jobs}` (empty array if no printers) or `{success:false, error}`. - `buildMenuSalesPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive, periodLabel)` — same pattern but queries `transaction_items` joined `transactions!inner`, aggregates by item name (qty, amount), builds ticket via `buildMenuSalesTicket`. - Return type: `BuildReportPrintResult = {success:true; jobs: KitchenPrintJobPayload[]} | {success:false; error:string}` - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-buttons.tsx`** (NEW file, shared client component) - `"use client"`, takes `{businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive, periodLabel}` props - Two buttons "🖨️ Cetak Settlement" / "🖨️ Cetak Laporan Menu", each with independent `State` (idle/sending/ok/empty/error), calling the corresponding action then `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, built.jobs)` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs` - Renders inline ✅/empty/❌ feedback per button, mirroring the established `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` pattern - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/reports/page.tsx`** - Added import: `import ReportPrintButtons from "../../report-print-buttons";` - Added a new "🖨️ Cetak Laporan" card right before the existing "⬇️ Ekspor Data" card: ```tsx

🖨️ Cetak Laporan

``` - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/reports/page.tsx`** (NEW file, created to fix the "Laporan not visible in Android app" gap) - Server Component, mirrors `pos/printers/page.tsx`'s gating pattern exactly: fetch business, then `getCashierSession(businessId)` — if no session, render `PinScreen` with cashier list; otherwise render `` - Full content already written (see analysis section above for complete code) — this file is NOT gated by `isNative`, making it reachable from the Android app menu, unlike `(dashboard)/reports/page.tsx`. - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/reports/report-print-screen.tsx`** (NEW file) - Client component with local period-selector state (not URL-driven, since this is a standalone quick screen): buttons for Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua + Kustom (with two `` fields for from/to) - Computes `{fromIso, toIsoExclusive}` via `getPeriodRange(period, customFrom, customTo)` and a `periodLabel` (custom range shows as "YYYY-MM-DD s/d YYYY-MM-DD" or the from-date alone if same day) - Renders `` inside a card, with a back link to `/business/${businessId}/pos` and a footer note about auto-targeting the `prints_receipt` printer - Full content already written (see analysis section above). - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/reports/period.ts`** (read only, not modified) — confirmed exports: `Period` type, `PERIOD_COOKIE_NAME`, `PERIOD_LABELS`, `PERIOD_DESCRIPTIONS`, `REPORT_TIMEZONE`, `parsePeriod()`, `getPeriodRange(period, customFrom?, customTo?): {fromIso, toIsoExclusive}` — all pure, no `"use server"`/`"use client"` directive, safe to import from anywhere. - **`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/printers/page.tsx`** (read only, used as the reference pattern) — confirms the exact PIN-gating shape mirrored for the new `pos/reports/page.tsx`. 4. Errors and fixes: - **User report "di HP blm ada perubahan sama sekali, masih KARTU dan tidak ada settlement nya"**: Initially suspected the same device-cache issue seen repeatedly earlier in the session, but direct verification against the LIVE production URL (fresh browser tab, `https://createimpact.id`, logged in as `claude.test.reports@gmail.com` / `test-kasirku-123`) showed the SAME stale "Kartu" content — ruling out a device-only cache problem. Ran `npm run build` locally — succeeded cleanly with no errors, ruling out a build failure. Asked user to check the Vercel dashboard directly (`AskUserQuestion`). User provided a screenshot of `vercel.com/melan1/kasirku/deployments` showing the deployments list topped by "Try insecure Bluetooth RFCOMM firs..." (commit `b3c19c5`, marked Production, Ready) — the "Add printable settlement + menu sales reports" commit (`1cc18dd`) was **completely absent** from the list, meaning Vercel never even attempted to build it (dropped GitHub webhook, not a build failure). **Fix**: created an empty commit `git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger redeploy — previous push (1cc18dd) never reached Vercel..."` and pushed (new commit `390aa91`) to force a fresh webhook delivery. User confirmed "oke ready" once the new deployment appeared and went Ready in Vercel. I then re-verified directly on production (fresh browser session): confirmed "EDC" now shows at checkout and both "🖨️ Cetak Settlement"/"🖨️ Cetak Laporan Menu" buttons now appear on the Reports page. - **User feedback "blm ada laporan"**: After I told the user the reprint feature lives on the "Laporan" (Reports) page reachable via POS Menu, the user sent a screenshot proving the Android app's actual POS Menu panel has NO "Laporan" entry at all. I investigated `pos-screen.tsx` and found the existing (pre-existing, not introduced by me) code: `{!isNative && (📊 Laporan)}` — confirming Laporan is deliberately hidden from native/Android sessions by design, consistent with project history ("Restrict the Android app to POS-only, no backoffice, like Moka's Cashier role"). # Printable shift settlement + menu sales report (by date)

## Context
User wants two new printable reports, closer to what Moka POS gives at shift close: a **settlement** report (Tunai/QRIS/EDC totals) and a **menu sales** report (item/qty sold) — both printable for any transaction date range, not just tied to a live shift. `close_shift`'s RPC only computes a cash-vs-non-cash split (`shift_rpc.sql:53-133`), and there's no per-method breakdown or print action anywhere in the codebase today (the shift-receipt route from an earlier now-reverted session doesn't exist). The Reports page (`reports/page.tsx`) already computes both aggregations in-memory for its date-filtered view (`byMethod` map, `menuSales` map) and already has CSV/Excel export buttons — that's the natural place to add "print" as a third export option, plus a convenience shortcut right after closing a shift.

Confirmed with user: "Kartu" is renamed to "EDC" (same slot, no schema change — old transactions keep showing "Kartu" as their recorded method, new ones record "EDC"); both reports auto-print to whichever printer(s) are flagged `prints_receipt` in Settings (same target as customer receipts), no printer picker needed.

## Approach

**1. Rename payment method label** — `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS` in `pos-screen.tsx:91` and its duplicate in `ticket-pos-screen.tsx`: `"Kartu"` → `"EDC"`.

**2. `src/lib/escpos.ts`** — two new ESC/POS ticket builders, following `buildReceiptTicket`'s existing shape/helpers (`padLine`, `RECEIPT_WIDTH`):
   - `buildSettlementTicket({businessName, periodLabel, byMethod: {method, amount}[], totalSales, txCount, voidCount})` — "LAPORAN SETTLEMENT" header, one line per payment method + total, tx/void counts.
   - `buildMenuSalesTicket({businessName, periodLabel, items: {name, qty, amount}[], totalQty, totalAmount})` — "LAPORAN PENJUALAN MENU" header, one line per item, sorted by amount desc (matches Reports page's existing "Menu Terlaris" ordering).

**3. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-actions.ts`** (business-level, not inside `(dashboard)` or `pos/`, so both can import it) — two server actions:
   - `buildSettlementPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   - `buildMenuSalesPrintJobs(businessId, fromIso, toIsoExclusive)`
   
   Each: finds `kitchen_printers` where `prints_receipt = true` (same query shape as `buildReceiptPrintJobsForTransaction` in `pos/actions.ts`), queries `transaction_payments`/`transaction_items` joined to `transactions` filtered by business+date range+`voided = false` (same filter pattern already used in `reports/page.tsx:92-101`), aggregates in JS (mirror the page's existing `byMethod`/`menuSales` reduce logic so the printed numbers always match what's on screen), builds one ticket via the new builders, and returns one `KitchenPrintJobPayload` per matching printer. Empty printer list → `{success:true, jobs:[]}`, handled as a "no printer configured" message client-side (same pattern as the existing reprint button's empty state).

**4. New `src/app/business/[businessId]/report-print-buttons.tsx`** (client component, shared) — takes `businessId`, `fromIso`, `toIsoExclusive` as props, renders two buttons ("🖨️ Cetak Settlement", "🖨️ Cetak Laporan Menu"), each calling its action then `dispatchPrintJobs` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs`, inline ✅/❌ state per button — same established pattern as `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx`.

**5. Wire into `reports/page.tsx`** — add `<ReportPrintButtons businessId={businessId} fromIso={fromIso} toIsoExclusive={toIsoExclusive} />` in a new small card right above/alongside the existing "⬇️ Ekspor Data" card, reusing the `fromIso`/`toIsoExclusive` already computed there via `getPeriodRange` — this alone satisfies "bisa cetak berdasarkan tanggal transaksi" for both reports, using the same date-range UI (Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua/Kustom) already on that page.

**6. Wire a shortcut into `pos-screen.tsx`'s shift-close success screen** (`closedSummary` block) — same `<ReportPrintButtons>`, scoped to "today" via `getPeriodRange("today")` imported from `reports/period.ts` (same WIB-correct day-boundary helper the Reports page already uses, avoids reinventing date math). This is a convenience shortcut, not shift-exact scoping (if a business runs multiple shifts same day, this prints the whole day, not just that shift — acceptable given the user's own framing centers on "berdasarkan tanggal transaksi", and the Reports page remains available for any other exact range).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`.
- Browser (dev test account): confirm "EDC" now shows at checkout instead of "Kartu". Configure a `prints_receipt` printer (mirroring earlier verified LAN/Bluetooth test flow), do a transaction, then hit both new print buttons on the Reports page — confirm a job gets built for the configured printer (will fail/queue in this environment since there's no real printer, same limitation as all prior printer testing this session — that's fine, proves the build+dispatch path).
- Confirm the numbers in the printed ticket's underlying aggregation match what's already shown on-screen for the same period (spot-check the byMethod/menuSales sums).
- Confirm the shift-close screen's shortcut buttons appear after closing a shift and target today's date range correctly.

Business "Toko Test Laporan" (F&B, id `7c483432-1c9a-4f03-a0b2-aa4d89f7f5e9`) with cashier "Melan" PIN `1234`, manager "Manajer Test" PIN `9999` (for void authorization), PPN 10% + service 5% enabled (affects checkout totals), products Kopi Susu/Roti Bakar, an open shift, 2 transactions on 2026-07-03, and table "Meja 1" (qr_slug `CWsFCMmosD7O`, id `8b67c355-65a2-47d3-a79a-a935ede87dd3`) for self-order testing. Self-orders can be seeded directly via REST insert into `self_orders` + `self_order_items` using the owner access token from the browser cookie (`sb-…-auth-token`, base64 JSON) since the customer-facing RPC is still missing on remote (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]). Safe to reuse or delete — it's a separate auth user, invisible to the real owner account.

12	Same owner account also has a ticket-venue business "Kolam Renang Test" (id `f43c8529-7fe5-4074-9e98-43335da31267`, 🎟️ Tempat Wisata/Tiket) with cashier "Kasir Tiket" (role manajer) — PIN reset to `1234` on 2026-07-07 via Kelola Kasir (original PIN unknown), an open shift, ticket categories Pengunjung/Rp25.000/Penunggu/Rp10.000/Yoga clas/Rp340.000, and members "Budi Member" (M-0001) plus test-added "Budi Tester" (MBR-001, member_price Rp0 for Pengunjung). Confirmed working end-to-end: manual physical ticket numbers on checkout (duplicate number correctly rejected with a friendly error), member lookup/pricing in POS, ticket-reports reconciliation list, CSV export (`/ticket-reports/export?type=transactions&period=today`), member barcode card (`/members/<id>/card`, uses jsbarcode), and transaction detail/void page.
13	
14	**IMPORTANT UPDATE 2026-07-17 — this account lives on the PRODUCTION Supabase project only.** Since the dev/prod split ([[supabase-dev-prod-split]]), local `.env.local` points at "KasirKu Dev", where this account does NOT exist. A separate dev-DB test account was created there via the admin API: `claude.test.dev@example.com` / `test-kasirku-dev-123`, business "Toko Test Dev" (F&B, id `b93a088f-15c3-4147-b29a-1342235ab855`, subscription manually set to `lifetime`/`active` via service-role), cashier "Kasir Dev" (role manajer, PIN `1234`), product "Kopi Susu Dev" (Rp15.000, cost Rp6.000), one completed cash transaction INV-20260716-0001. Use THIS account for local preview verification from now on; the paragraph above only applies if deliberately testing against production.

17	
18	**How to apply:** log in at /login with these credentials, then navigate to /business/<id>/... pages. Note: Turbopack on the slow G: drive sometimes serves stale CSS after globals.css edits — `rm -rf .next` and restart the dev server if new Tailwind utilities don't apply. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]]. **Bigger version of the same flakiness (hit 2026-07-14, see [[finance-standalone-product]] Fase 3)**: adding a brand-new nested route folder can make *every other* route in that `(dashboard)` group 404, even after one `rm -rf .next` + restart — needs a **second** full stop+clear+restart cycle to pick up the new route tree correctly on this drive. If unrelated sibling routes suddenly 404 right after adding a new page file, restart again before assuming the new code is broken. The POS PIN keypad (pin-screen.tsx) is plain React state, not a real input — driving it with `preview_eval` by firing all 4 digit clicks in one synchronous block silently fails (React batches the clicks and reads a stale `pin` closure each time, so it never reaches length 4 and neither succeeds nor shows an error). Use separate calls per digit, one per tool call, so each click gets its own render cycle. **Update 2026-07-10**: even one-at-a-time, the `preview_click` *tool* (as opposed to `preview_eval`) reliably failed to register on these digit buttons at all — no server action ever fired (confirmed via server logs showing zero `verifyPin` calls), tried across a fresh page load, multiple reloads, and 1-3s waits between clicks. Switching each digit press to `preview_eval` with `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.grid.grid-cols-3.gap-3 button')).find(b => b.textContent.trim() === '<digit>').click()` worked on the very first attempt. If `preview_click` ever seems unresponsive on this keypad (or similar plain-onClick grids) again, don't assume the PIN/credentials are wrong — switch to the `preview_eval` `.click()` approach first.
